findings.text: the plan comment reads 'The declared mutation — removing the hostname field from the emitted payload — makes the named test fail with …', presenting a shortened transcription as the declared text, where the declared line reads 'remove the hostname field from the payload emitted by the throttling sampler; the test asserting that the payload names the host it was read on must then be observed to fail'. The same shortened form is italicised as the declared mutation at docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html:774-776. Both documents were authored by this node in its own landing commit, one pass after it repaired exactly this defect in the negative-control receipt (the repair is disclosed in its own manifest), so the rule it applied to its receipt was not applied to the two documents the same node wrote. Both passages are introduced by a phrase that claims to state the declared mutation, which is what makes a paraphrase here worse than an omission: a reader has no way to tell the quoted sentence is not the authority. Pointing at the declared-mutation file in both places removes the second copy rather than correcting it.

read_host() is exercised by no test. The payload-level injection the change added is used by every test, so the values the new fields carry are asserted over a fixture machine, but the three machine reads behind them and the host=None branch of main(argv, host=None) are demonstrated only against the live host. The read is substitutable without restructuring — _BOOT_ID_FILE and _UPTIME_FILE are module constants looked up at call time, and a patched pair was measured here to drive the real function to both of its refusal paths — so one test that monkeypatches the two paths and the hostname covers the wiring the change exists to establish, and it is the only part of the new code a node in this cluster could break without the suite noticing.

parse_boot_id refuses only emptiness: 'not-a-uuid' is accepted and reported as the boot identity (measured). The refusal is named 'boot_id is empty', which is accurate about what it checks; the gap is that nothing distinguishes the kernel's identifier from any other non-blank string, so a node whose file carried a stale or substituted value would be reported as a boot rather than refused. On this cluster the value is always the kernel's, so this is a robustness note rather than a defect in the shipped behaviour, and the honest boundary is the one the module already draws for cpu.stat, where fields the change does not name are ignored rather than refused.

the live-read payload quoted in the landing record (the host block at lines 829-836: hostname 98dci4-srv-1006.iter.org, boot_id 82c41dfa-a445-4fb2-8416-04b44c3d874c, uptime 3798078.02; the share 0.3373 at line 849) is not backed by a captured log: the run directory holds only logs/throttle_test_final.log and logs/throttle_ruff_post.log, and the manifest's test_logs name paths outside the run directory, which do not survive the session. An independent read here reproduces the substance — the same boot_id, uptime 3799941.83 s, so one uninterrupted boot and the same 43 d 23 h age — so the figure is sound and the deduction is traceability: an artifact that will not survive the session is a weaker receipt than the run's own logs directory is.

the record's Scope paragraph files the change under imas_ambix/agent/test_throttling.py, where the test file is tests/agent/test_throttling.py. A path a reader follows to check the claim leads nowhere, which is the mechanical half of the same defect the receipt was repaired for: the prose is right about intent and wrong about the string.

item_verdicts.negative_control: verified as a receipt rather than as an absence of error: the first line of /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/fleet-throttling-host-negative-control.log is byte-identical to line 1 of its authority file (a string comparison and a sha256 comparison, both 7e680a49c866e6ad1b31306fb047914cd158fc4395f7981ce870ff79501a5cee), the log records the applied diff, the named test failing with KeyError: 'hostname' at the assertion rather than at collection, and the restore to green in the same log. The mutation reaches the behaviour the change adds: removing 'hostname' from _host_payload makes the payload-names-the-host test fail.
item_verdicts.question_a_payload_alone_distinguishes_m: VERDICT: YES. Evidence: the payload carries host{hostname, boot_id, uptime_seconds} at the top level of both subcommands (tests/agent/test_throttling.py:384 and :439 pin the exact sets, so nothing can be added or removed silently); hostname comes from socket.gethostname() and is therefore the machine, not the operand — which is the point, since /sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-39486.slice is a valid operand on every node in the cluster with different contents; boot_id is the kernel's fresh-per-boot UUID, so two payloads differing in counters but not in boot identity describe one uninterrupted counter run, and this is the case the change exists for: throttled_usec and permitted_usec are cumulative since boot, so both fall at a restart and their ratio falls with them, making a reboot read as a sudden improvement. Verified live and independently here: read_host() on this login node returns boot_id 82c41dfa-a445-4fb2-8416-04b44c3d874c with uptime 3799941.83 s against the reviewed run's own read of the same boot_id at uptime 3798078.02 s, so the same identifier is carried across readings while the age advances. No out-of-band knowledge is required of the reader: the three field names state what they settle, and a reader comparing two payloads needs nothing but the two payloads.
item_verdicts.question_b_read_path_testable_or_live_on: VERDICT: PARTLY — the values are exercised by tests, the machine read is not. Evidence: the injection seam works and is used — main(argv, host=None) takes the identity as the control group is taken, calls read_host() only when host is None, and all four TestMain call sites pass the fixture _HOST, so the payload shape and every value behind it are asserted over a known machine rather than over whatever host the suite runs on; parse_uptime and parse_boot_id are pure text-to-value functions covered directly (7 and 4 tests, including the blank and non-numeric refusals). What is NOT exercised: read_host() is named by no test (a grep over tests/agent/test_throttling.py at the reviewed head returns zero hits), so the wiring from socket.gethostname(), /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and /proc/uptime into HostIdentity — and the default host=None branch of main — is demonstrated only against the live machine. The read is testable without restructuring: the two paths are module constants resolved at call time, and a patched pair was measured here to drive the real function to both of its refusal paths (blank text to ValueError 'boot_id is empty', a missing file to FileNotFoundError). So the accurate statement is that the design makes the read substitutable and the suite does not substitute it — one test short of the record's claim that the fields are asserted over a fixture, which is true of the fields as VALUES and unproven as a READ.
item_verdicts.question_c_wire_contract_extended_or_loo: VERDICT: EXTENDED DELIBERATELY, NOT LOOSENED. Evidence: the pre-existing pin is an equality against a literal set and is still an equality against a literal set — the sample subcommand's assertion moved from {'directory','cpu_max','cumulative'} to {'directory','host','cpu_max','cumulative'} (tests/agent/test_throttling.py:384), which fails on an addition as well as on a removal, and the interval subcommand's top-level set likewise gained exactly 'host' (:439) while its nested interval key set is unchanged. The counters payload's own _EXPECTED_KEYS is byte-identical before and after (the pre-change and post-change blocks diffed clean, and the assertion at :330 still compares against it). Nothing was softened into an issubset, a membership test or a subset comparison. The test diff's deletions are exactly the four call sites that now pass the fixture plus that one literal, so no pre-existing assertion was dropped. One caveat for a monitor rather than a loosening: the added key sits at the TOP level of both subcommands, so a consumer that counts top-level keys or compares whole payloads sees one new sibling key — the class of change a consumer reading named keys absorbs without change — and the module's published usage remains a subprocess read that prints the object.
item_verdicts.question_d_absent_or_malformed_field_on_: VERDICT: no field can be silently absent, and the reader fails loud — with one shape gap and one container caveat. Evidence, measured on this login node rather than reasoned: /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and /proc/uptime both exist on this node's kernel; blank boot_id text raises ValueError 'boot_id is empty'; non-numeric uptime raises ValueError 'uptime is not a number'; a path that does not exist raises FileNotFoundError. Each propagates out of read_host() and out of main() before any payload is printed, so the failure mode is a non-zero exit with a traceback and NO reading rather than a reading whose host block is empty or placeholder — the correct direction, because a payload without provenance is precisely what the change exists to prevent, and it keeps the module's existing contract that a value is either real or an explicit cause, as throttled_share does with 'unbounded' and 'no_periods' spellings. The gap: parse_boot_id refuses only emptiness, so 'not-a-uuid' is accepted as a boot identity and the JSON type is a plain string, so a monitor can compare boot ids but cannot validate that they are kernel identifiers; on this cluster the value always is one, since the kernel writes it. The caveat: /proc/uptime and boot_id are the KERNEL's rather than a namespace's, so a sampler run inside a container reads the host's boot identity and age beside the container's hostname — internally inconsistent in a way nothing in the payload marks; no use of this sampler on this cluster is containerised, so this is a limit of the instrument rather than a defect in the change, and it is worth one line in the module rather than a guard.

justifications.durability: the new guards are committed and were seen to fire, not inferred: the declared mutation was applied and the named test observed red at the assertion rather than at collection, so a regression that drops the field from the payload is caught by the suite. The added tests are property-shaped rather than spelling checks — the reboot test asserts a property of two payloads (different boot_id, lower uptime) rather than an expectation about one, and the parser tests refuse blank and non-numeric text with ValueError rather than accepting it. Docked for three measured gaps: (a) read_host() is called by no test in the suite — every one of the four main(...) call sites passes the injected fixture, so the default host=None branch and the three machine reads behind it are exercised only live; the read IS testable by monkeypatching the module's _BOOT_ID_FILE and _UPTIME_FILE, which was demonstrated here (a patched path holding blank text raises ValueError 'boot_id is empty'; a patched path that does not exist raises FileNotFoundError), so the capability exists unused rather than absent; (b) parse_boot_id validates presence, not shape — measured here, the string 'not-a-uuid' is accepted as a boot identity, so nothing can distinguish a kernel identifier from any other non-blank string; (c) malformed input to the READ path is uncaught at the CLI boundary: the machine reads happen before the reading is taken, so a node whose file is absent or truncated produces a traceback and no payload at all rather than a reading whose host block is marked unavailable. That last behaviour is defensible — failing loud beats emitting a reading whose provenance is unknown, which is the failure this change exists to prevent — but it is a new dependency of a command whose only prior dependency was the caller's directory, and it is stated nowhere.
justifications.evidence: strong where it matters and imprecise where it does not. Verified here by reading the artifacts rather than the claims: the red log /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/fleet-throttling-host-negative-control.log has line 1 byte-identical to line 1 of its authority file fleet-sample-host-declared-mutation.txt (a string comparison and a sha256 comparison, both 7e680a49c866e6ad1b31306fb047914cd158fc4395f7981ce870ff79501a5cee), the log records the applied git diff, the named test failing KeyError: 'hostname' at the assertion rather than at collection, and the restore to green in the same log; the focused suite re-runs here at 48 passed exit 0 and the whole-tree lint at exit 0. Three deductions, all about the record rather than the code: (1) the plan comment and the evidence record, BOTH authored by this node in 16b5331d, present a shortened transcription as the declared text — the plan at docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html:429 reads 'The declared mutation — removing the hostname field from the emitted payload — makes the named test fail with …', and the evidence record at docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html:774-776 italicises 'remove the hostname field from the emitted payload', against the declared line's 'remove the hostname field from the payload emitted by the throttling sampler; the test asserting that the payload names the host it was read on must then be observed to fail' — so the node repaired exactly this class of error in its receipt one pass earlier and then reproduced it in the two documents it wrote; (2) the live-read payload quoted in both documents is not backed by a captured log — the run directory holds only logs/throttle_test_final.log and logs/throttle_ruff_post.log, and the manifest's test_logs name paths outside the run directory — so the quoted 0.3373 reading is reproducible but was not captured; an independent re-read here does reproduce the substance (same boot_id 82c41dfa-a445-4fb2-8416-04b44c3d874c, uptime advanced from 3798078.02 s to 3799941.83 s, so one uninterrupted boot), which is why this is a traceability deduction and not a wrong-result one; (3) the landing record's Scope paragraph files the change under imas_ambix/agent/test_throttling.py, where the file is tests/agent/test_throttling.py — a reader following that path to check the claim finds nothing.
justifications.fit: the change is placed where the plan needs it and follows the conventions of the module it extends. It is additive at the wire level: one added top-level key on both subcommands with nothing moved, so a monitor reading named keys sees no change, and the module keeps its own _parser()/main() entry point so a consumer can read a slice as a subprocess. The host identity is injected through the same seam as the control group — main(argv, host=None) — which preserves the existing contract that the caller decides what is measured, and the three values come from their authoritative sources (socket.gethostname(), /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, the first field of /proc/uptime) rather than being inferred from the counters. It uses the kernel's per-boot identifier rather than a boot timestamp, which is the stronger choice: a fresh UUID per boot cannot collide the same way a coarse timestamp can. No plan, sprint or ticket identifiers and no version suffixes appear in any added symbol, comment or filename.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the stated purpose — two readings taken on different machines, or on one machine across a reboot, being distinguishable from the payload ALONE — is met and was measured here, not read: the emitted object carries host{hostname,boot_id,uptime_seconds} at the top level of BOTH subcommands (verified in the committed revision by the equality sets at tests/agent/test_throttling.py:384 and :439, and by an independent live read of this login node through the committed module), the kernel supplies boot_id and uptime rather than the sampler inferring them, and the reboot case is the one the payload makes legible: boot_id changes and uptime restarts, so a cumulative share that fell is attributable rather than merely suspicious: throttled_usec and permitted_usec are cumulative since boot, so both fall at a restart and the ratio fell with them, reading as a sudden improvement — which is the comparison the plan's step seven rests on (docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html, the step whose done-when is the login slice's throttled fraction over a working day against the section 2 baseline). Docked one point because the payload names the machine the SAMPLER ran on through the kernel's own view, so a reading taken inside a container would report the container's hostname beside the host kernel's boot_id and uptime — correct for every use this cluster makes of it, since the sampler runs as an ordinary user process against the account's own slice, but unnamed as a limit in the record.
justifications.scope_discipline: the two commits touch exactly the declared write paths — 7a52e6e2 the sampler and its tests (204 insertions across 2 files), 16b5331d the two landing documents (147 insertions across 2 files) — with no edit to imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py, imas_ambix/agent/cli.py or tests/agent/test_fleet.py, which the run manifest names as its unedited neighbours. No AI attribution, conventional subjects with bodies that state what changed and why. The one item I would not call a scope violation but a scope judgement worth naming is recorded under evidence: the shortened declared-mutation transcription carries into a document this node authored, and the node then reported its own two-document copy of that text as a follow_on rather than fixing it, which is the advised split because the repair pass forbade document edits — but it leaves the defect standing in prose the same node wrote, and a two-line pointer would have removed the second copy of the sentence rather than correcting it.

raw_text: Review of run r-20260921T090055615010-fleet-sample-names-its-host, plan imas-ambix:slurm-hosted-agent-fleet section 7 (the throttling reading that section 2's baseline and the step comparing the login slice over a working day rest on). Landed change: 7a52e6e2 (HostIdentity, parse_uptime, parse_boot_id, read_host, _host_payload, a host block in the emitted payload, and an injected host argument on main, with 26 new tests) and 16b5331d (the landing record in the plan comment and the evidence document); base 0dcf297d0fd0b2019cad02f1d4ec64bb9f960acc, head 16b5331d7f24ba6ec45e6d60f0fe343cc71b2675. Read for this review: both commit diffs against the base, the reviewed run's live pointer, manifest, negative-control receipt and its authority file, the plan sections 2 and 7 and the plan comment the node added, the evidence record, tests/agent/test_throttling.py at the reviewed head, and the run directory's logs; plus an independent live read of this login node through the committed module and a probe of read_host's refusal paths. Reproduced here: pytest tests/agent/test_throttling.py 48 passed exit 0 in 0.31s, and ruff check --no-cache imas_ambix tests 'All checks passed!' exit 0. THE FOUR QUESTIONS, each with its verdict recorded above in item_verdicts: (a) YES — the payload alone distinguishes two machines (hostname from the socket, not from the operand, which resolves on every node with different contents) and two boots (a fresh-per-boot kernel UUID, with the uptime making the difference legible rather than merely detectable); the reboot case is load-bearing because throttled_usec and permitted_usec are cumulative since boot, so both counters and their ratio fall at a restart and a drop previously read as recovery; confirmed by an independent live read returning the same boot_id as the reviewed run's own reading with the uptime advanced. (b) PARTLY — the values are asserted over a fixture through the same seam the control group uses and the two parsers are covered directly, but read_host() is named by no test, so the default host=None branch is live-only; the read is substitutable by monkeypatching two module constants, which was demonstrated here, so the design is right and the covering test is the thing missing. (c) EXTENDED DELIBERATELY — the pins remain equality against a literal set on both subcommands, the counters key set is byte-identical before and after, and the test diff's only deleted assertions are the call sites and the one literal that gained 'host', so the monitor's contract was widened by exactly one sibling key and nothing was relaxed into a subset test. (d) NO FIELD CAN BE SILENTLY ABSENT — the reader raises on blank boot_id, non-numeric uptime and a missing file, and because the reads precede the payload the result is no payload and a non-zero exit rather than a reading with unknown provenance, which is the right direction; two limits recorded rather than fixed: parse_boot_id validates presence and not shape, and the boot identity and uptime are the kernel's rather than a namespace's, so a containerised sampler would pair the container's hostname with the host's boot. One earlier deduction was WITHDRAWN after it failed to reproduce at review time: the run manifest's commits field resolves correctly, and the non-resolving tail it was scored against appears only inside the run's own stream (recorded under withdrawn_checks with the check that cleared it). Scoring: goal_fidelity 19 (the stated purpose met and measured; one point for the container asymmetry going unnamed), evidence 15 (the negative-control receipt is exact and verified against its authority by hash and the gates reproduce; deductions for the shortened declared-mutation transcription presented as the declared text in both documents this node authored, a live-read figure quoted without a captured log, and a module path that does not exist in the Scope paragraph), durability 15 (guards committed and seen to fire, tests property-shaped; gaps: read_host untested, boot_id shape unvalidated, malformed input to the read path uncaught at the CLI boundary and unstated), fit 18 (additive key, the module's own seam, the kernel's authoritative sources, no plan labels), scope_discipline 18 (exactly the declared paths across both commits, no neighbouring surface touched, the two-document transcription defect reported as a follow_on rather than edited in a pass that left document edits out of scope). No item in this change is a correctness defect in shipped behaviour: all four answered questions are satisfied or satisfied-with-a-named-limit, and the deductions are record fidelity and test coverage rather than wrong results.
withdrawn_checks: WITHDRAWN, verified not to reproduce at review time: an earlier pass of this review recorded that the reviewed run's manifest commits field carried 16b5331d7f24ba6ec45e6d60f0fe343cc71b2672, a string that is not a valid object. At review time the manifest's commits list reads ["7a52e6e2b0f9f1016f979ef2cb1097ab27da05dd", "16b5331d7f24ba6ec45e6d60f0fe343cc71b2675"] (manifest.md:11) and resolves; the non-resolving tail appears once in the run's own stream inside an in-flight tool call, never in a delivered field, and a scan of the branch's commit messages finds it nowhere. Withdrawn as a finding, and the deduction returned to the score.
